entrypoints.summary: The public PHP endpoint reads GET msg, accepts it when its byte length is at most 30, and executes a SQLite statement constructed with that value.
The supplied author exploit exercises the endpoint through HTTP GET requests carrying a URL-encoded msg payload.

negative_controls: No captured response content, status assertion, or fixed-target control is included.
observability.positive_marker: The exploit prints the content returned after requesting p.php?o=id.

preconditions: The target runs the shown PHP SQLite endpoint with the Docker filesystem layout.
The attacker can send repeated requests that resolve to the same remote-address-derived sandbox.
The SQL payload must fit the endpoint's msg length condition.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: ');VACUUM INTO('... with a filename or fragment selected to remain within the length constraint.
trigger_steps.summary: Send a quote-closing msg payload with VACUUM INTO and a short attacker-selected filename to materialize staged fragments.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: GET to the served sandbox file with query parameter o=id.
trigger_steps.summary: Request the staged p.php with o=id after constructing its PHP shell content.

capabilities.concept: SQLite VACUUM INTO arbitrary file creation

relation_candidates.rationale: msg is interpolated into the SQL source text, and the author payload closes the literal before appending SQL syntax.

relation_candidates.dst: SQLite VACUUM INTO arbitrary file creation
relation_candidates.rationale: The author payload uses injected VACUUM INTO with selected filenames, and the application sandbox is under the Apache document tree.
The exploit stages PHP shell fragments into p.php and requests it with o=id.
relation_candidates.src: SQLite VACUUM INTO arbitrary file creation

relation_candidates.rationale: VACUUM INTO is used to materialize attacker-selected files inside a served sandbox.
relation_candidates.src: SQLite VACUUM INTO arbitrary file creation

relation_candidates.rationale: The container installs a setuid helper that opens and writes /flag on its successful branch. Whether the supplied webshell sequence completes the helper's interactive arithmetic exchange is not shown.
Binding msg as a value removes its ability to terminate the intended SQL literal and introduce VACUUM INTO syntax.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of files below the Apache-served writable sandbox and confidentiality of the root-owned /flag through /read_flag.
impact.attacker_capability: Send length-constrained HTTP msg payloads that introduce SQLite VACUUM INTO syntax, construct a served PHP webshell over multiple requests, and invoke a shell command through that webshell.
impact.security_effect: Remote SQL statement injection can be converted into staged creation of attacker-controlled served PHP content and command execution; the provisioned setuid helper makes protected /flag disclosure plausibly reachable after command execution.

causal_trace.summary: A remote requester controls GET msg subject only to a 30-byte length check; processing occurs after changing into a sandbox derived from the requester's remote address.

The application places msg directly inside the quoted VALUES expression of a SQL string passed to SQLite3::exec, so untrusted text can terminate the intended literal and become SQLite syntax rather than remaining one text value.
The author payload closes the VALUES literal and appends VACUUM INTO with attacker-selected short filenames. Repeated requests stage fragments and create PHP files below the served sandbox path.

The staged p.php is requested with o=id and is constructed to execute its o parameter as a shell command. The container also provides a setuid read_flag helper that reads /flag and writes its bytes when supplied the correct arithmetic answer; using web command execution to drive that helper is an environmental reachability inference, not an observed end-to-end run in the supplied exploit.

failure.operation: SQLite3::exec executes a dynamically formatted INSERT statement containing the attacker-controlled msg value.

primary_invariant.statement: The msg parameter must be supplied to SQLite as a single data value and must not alter statement syntax or select a database export filename.
primary_invariant.violated_because: sprintf interpolates msg into a quoted SQL INSERT and SQLite3::exec receives the resulting statement text; the supplied payload demonstrates quote termination followed by VACUUM INTO syntax.

quality.review_notes: Primary application source, Docker configuration, author exploit, and privileged-reader source were inspected. The author exploit contains request code and prints responses but the bundle contains no captured successful execution result. It explicitly demonstrates an id webshell request, not a completed /read_flag interaction; flag disclosure is therefore recorded as a strongly supported reachability inference. No upstream patch or fixed revision is present.

remediation.invariant_restored: Bind msg as a SQLite value rather than incorporating it into statement text; additionally ensure database-generated files cannot be created in an Apache-served writable directory and do not expose a setuid flag-reading helper to the web-process environment.
mitigation_classes: disable or constrain database export/write primitives
separate writable paths from web-served paths
remove web-process reachability to privileged helpers

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The requester must target the same remote-address-derived sandbox across staged HTTP requests; the author solution first invokes reset and then builds shell fragments under the known local sandbox path.
data_structure_invariants: msg is intended to occupy one TEXT value in INSERT INTO msg VALUES('...').
The application-created .db is removed after each request, while files materialized by injected VACUUM INTO can persist in the sandbox.
The Docker configuration makes /www/sandbox writable and makes /www point to the Apache document root.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The endpoint accepts msg only when strlen(msg) is at most 30; the supplied exploit asserts each injected payload is shorter than 32 bytes.
numeric_domains.name: msg length
numeric_domains.width: byte length measured by PHP strlen

state_context.state_machine: Each qualifying msg request changes into a deterministic per-client sandbox, creates .db, executes the constructed SQL, closes the database, and unlinks .db. The author sequence issues multiple requests to leave VACUUM-generated artifacts despite that .db cleanup.

target.component: PHP index endpoint and its per-client SQLite sandbox
target.language: PHP with SQLite SQL; deployed with Apache

oracle.expected_negative: No patched implementation or captured negative-control execution is supplied; a parameterized implementation should treat the payload as stored text rather than execute appended SQLite syntax.
oracle.expected_positive: Against the shown vulnerable application, the supplied staged HTTP sequence is intended to retrieve the generated p.php with o=id, whose constructed PHP evaluates that parameter as a shell command.
